title: In the beginning (Genesis 1:1–5)
hookLine: darkness on the deep, the Spirit over the waters, and let there be light

lines: THE EASTER VIGIL, IN THE DARK.
ONE CANDLE, THEN A ROOM OF THEM.
cards: It's the night before Easter, and the church is completely dark. People stand in the doorway holding unlit candles.
Outside, a fire is struck, a single tall candle is lit from it, and a deacon carries it slowly up the aisle, singing. The flame passes from wick to wick until the whole room glows.
Then everyone sits, and the first reading of that long night begins. Of all the pages in the library, the Church reads this one first, in the dark: the opening of Genesis. Bereshit.

teach.b: The Douay-Rheims, the old Catholic English translation, opens like this: "In the beginning God created heaven, and earth."
In Hebrew, in the beginning is a single word, bereshit, and it gives the whole book its Hebrew name. And the scene isn't tidy at all.

teach.h: SPIRIT, WIND, BREATH OVER THE DEEP.
teach.b: The earth is void and empty, darkness is on the face of the deep, and the spirit of God moves over the waters. The Hebrew for spirit, ruach, also means wind and breath.
So before anything has a shape, something is already moving over the dark water.

teach.h: BE LIGHT MADE. AND LIGHT WAS MADE.
teach.b: Then God speaks, and the line is well-known for how short it is: "Be light made. And light was made." A three-word command, and the result in four. No battle, no raw material wrestled into shape.
A word, and then light. God sees that the light is good, separates it from the darkness, and calls one day and the other night. Easy to miss: the sun and moon don't appear until the fourth day.
Light comes before anything that shines. The Catechism teaches that the world begins in God's wisdom and love, not in accident or struggle.
Catholics hear the same opening at Christmas, in the Gospel of John: in the beginning was the Word.
And at the Vigil, on the night the Church celebrates the resurrection, the readings go back to the first light.

how: At the Easter Vigil, the first of the Old Testament readings is the creation account from Genesis 1, read in a church lit by candles from the new Easter fire.

o: a blessing said over the Easter fire
in the beginning, the Bible's first word
the Hebrew name for the first day

games.q: what's inside the first lines — tap the pairs.
p: in the beginning, one Hebrew word

s: in Genesis 1 the sun is made on the first day
the sun and moon come on the fourth day. light comes first, before anything that shines.
Genesis 1 is the first reading at the Easter Vigil
the Church reads it in the dark, by candlelight, on the night before Easter.
the Hebrew word for spirit also means wind and breath
ruach: wind, breath, spirit, moving over the waters.

games.q: the earth is void and empty, and darkness is on the face of the deep. what is the first thing God does?
o: God fights the dark waters and wins.
God makes the sun to light the world.
games.why: a word, and light: "Be light made. And light was made." no battle, and the sun doesn't come until day four.

practice: Sit for a moment in whatever dimness the room gives you, and notice what the dark does: the edges go soft, the room gets quieter.
Then reach for a lamp or a switch, slowly, and watch what appears: colors, faces in photos, the mess on the table, all of it there the whole time.
If you pray, say the old line silently, be light made; if not, just notice the difference light makes.

wordCard.voice: Bereshit, the Bible's first word, and the Hebrew name of Genesis. Before anything, God speaking light into the dark.
